findings.title: Infrastructure, Weather, and Station Health Monitoring
findings.summary: Railway controllers and station managers both require real-time visibility into track conditions, signalling faults, power supply, engineering works, live weather updates, and station accessibility facilities such as lifts and escalators.
findings.rationale: Direct alignment between controllers and station staff on the need for real-time operational status dashboards.

findings.title: Real-Time Train Manifests and Journey States
findings.summary: Station managers expect a real-time manifest of early trains and pre-planned changes, while controllers highlight the need to track detailed journey states like incident-affected, stationary, awaiting recovery, and evacuation underway.
findings.rationale: Both findings concern the tracking and display of train operational states and schedules, looking at it from station operations and network control perspectives respectively.

findings.title: Platform Changes and Station Staff Resistance
findings.summary: Controller-initiated platform changes can conflict with station staff concerns regarding accessibility, overcrowding, and insufficient notification time, posing safety and passenger experience issues.
findings.unresolved_question: How should the system handle a veto or warning raised by station staff against a controller-initiated platform change?
findings.rationale: Direct operational conflict between automated or controller-led routing and station-level constraints/accessibility requirements.

findings.title: Operational vs Commercial and Priority Trade-Offs
findings.summary: Competing priorities exist between TOC service maintenance, infrastructure safety, freight service priorities versus passenger diversions, and commercial versus operational cancellation boundaries.
findings.unresolved_question: Can an operational cancellation be triggered automatically if a TOC fails to confirm resource availability by a specific threshold time?
findings.rationale: Groups multiple stakeholder and priority conflicts regarding conflicting resource demands, safety obligations, and commercial decisions.

findings.title: Late Cancellation Notifications and Passenger Impact
findings.summary: Late notification of cancellations leads to passengers waiting unnecessarily, raising questions on automated alerts to reduce the notification window.
findings.unresolved_question: What automated alerts can reduce the window between a cancellation decision and passenger notification?
findings.rationale: Highlights a critical failure scenario centered around timing and communication gaps.

findings.title: Unclear Authority and Manual Override Procedures
findings.summary: Unclear authority during cancellations, data discrepancies between system predictions and visual reality, and the lack of a defined manual override procedure create ambiguity in operational decision-making.
findings.unresolved_question: What is the formal procedure and audit trail for overriding incorrect automated system predictions?
findings.rationale: Combines issues concerning authority, command hierarchies, and manual corrections when system predictions mismatch reality.

findings.title: Strict Audit Logging and Comprehensive Data Archiving
findings.summary: All decisions, instructions, authorizations, communications, and real-time transit data must be logged with precise timestamps and identities for later analysis and security compliance.
findings.rationale: Consistently aligned requirements around audit trails, logging, and data archiving.

findings.title: Passenger Information Systems Integration and Business Process Flows
findings.summary: System updates must integrate with Passenger Information Systems, station staff terminals, and respect the multi-party operational authorization flow involving controllers, signallers, staff, drivers, and TOCs.
findings.rationale: Both relate to core integration channels and multi-party stakeholder communication workflows.

findings.title: Automated Driver Route Competence Verification
findings.summary: Assumption that drivers are verified for route competence prior to authorization raises scope questions regarding whether route competence should be tracked automatically within the system.
findings.unresolved_question: Is driver route competence tracked automatically within the system or verified manually?
findings.rationale: Introduces an external competency check that could significantly expand system integration scope.

findings.title: Station Pre-Opening Physical Walk-Through
findings.summary: Station staff execute a manual pre-opening walk-through procedure to inspect physical infrastructure, ticket gates, amenities, and print out daily schedules.
findings.rationale: Important foundational station operations process that must be understood in system design.

findings.title: Input Mechanism for Locally Discovered Station Issues
findings.summary: It is currently ambiguous how station staff can input unprompted local incidents or infrastructure failures (e.g., broken ticket machine) into SmartRail for network-wide visibility.
findings.unresolved_question: Is there a dedicated local station status module for staff to input unprompted local incidents or infrastructure failures?
findings.rationale: Unique discovery regarding input mechanisms for station-specific faults that lacks a defined feature mapping.
